lines: +With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a package that runs a lifecycle script or has a patch is now cloned or copied into `node_modules`, as with the isolated linker. A build that rewrites one of its files no longer changes the store copy shared with other projects.
+Packages that an older pnpm version added to the store now run their install scripts. Before, pnpm could skip those scripts and hardlink the package's files to the store.

+On Windows, `packageImportMethod: auto` now tries hardlinking before cloning, as it does on Linux. Installs from a warm store on a Dev Drive are faster [#17809](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17809).
+On Windows, with `packageImportMethod: auto`, an install no longer fails when the store refuses a hardlink with an access-denied error. pnpm tries cloning or copying the file next.

Cloning, like copying, keeps `node_modules` separate from the store. You may edit files in your `node_modules` and they will not be modified in the central content-addressable store. Unlike a copy, a clone shares its data with the store file until one of them is written, so its contents take no extra disk space.
